segments.title: Benchmark ships frame the ideal destroyer
segments.body: The pictured ships provide benchmarks for considering an ideal destroyer in each period. Many of these examples are not necessarily the best destroyers of their generation. The comparison uses them to ask which capabilities would make a destroyer ideal for the conditions of its own era.

evidence.note: Pictured destroyers are period benchmarks for considering ideal capabilities, without necessarily being the best designs of their generation.

segments.summary: The ships shown are period benchmarks chosen to explain what an ideal destroyer required, not declarations that each pictured design was the best of its era.

segments.title: National roles shape destroyer design
segments.body: A destroyer suited to one navy may be a poor fit for another because each navy assigns it different duties. A fleet using destroyers chiefly as a shield may emphasize gun firepower. A navy treating them chiefly as an offensive spear may give torpedoes greater weight. A navy seeking general-purpose ships may add anti-submarine and minelaying capabilities alongside guns and torpedoes. National requirements can therefore lead to different choices even within the same generation.

evidence.note: Comparison of shield, spear, and general-purpose destroyer roles with their armament and capability priorities.

segments.summary: A destroyer optimized for fleet protection, offensive attack, or general-purpose duties will make different tradeoffs in guns, torpedoes, anti-submarine warfare, and minelaying.
